title: From Y to Z via Eta-Expansion
description: Compare the pure Y combinator with the call-by-value Z combinator that wraps x(x) in lambda v: x(x)(v) for strict evaluation in Python.

steps.description: Examine the pure Y combinator on line 1, where x(x) sits directly in the argument position of f(x(x)).

steps.question: What happens in Python if we call Y(f) with the pure Y combinator on line 1?
steps.answer: Python evaluates arguments before calling f, so x(x) calls itself immediately and triggers infinite recursion before f ever runs.

steps.description: Define Z by replacing x(x) with the eta-expanded wrapper lambda v: x(x)(v), which waits until an argument v is passed before evaluating x(x).
Apply Z to the factorial generator to create factorial_via_Z and print the factorials of 0 through 7.
Run the list comprehension on line 10 to see factorial_via_Z compute [1, 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, 720, 5040].
